subject.title: [BUG] memory index --force CLI writes incompatible meta providerKey, breaks runtime memory_search

question: Should memory_search keep failing closed on providerKey/scopeHash drift after CLI reindex, auto-repair known-safe identity drift, or move recovery into an explicit doctor/reindex migration path?
rationale: The remaining behavior is persisted memory/provider identity policy with upgrade and data-validity tradeoffs; source shows the fail-closed gates remain, while related reports show CLI and runtime can still disagree after partial fixes.

options.title: Add narrow identity repair or migration
options.body: Implement a tested repair path for known-safe CLI/runtime providerKey and scopeHash drift while preserving hard failure for genuinely incompatible indexes.

options.title: Keep fail-closed and improve diagnostics
options.body: Leave mismatch behavior strict but make the CLI/runtime instructions and logs prove exactly which provider/model/scope identity differs.

options.title: Warn-only runtime fallback
options.body: Allow runtime search to proceed on stale indexes after mismatch, accepting possible recall-quality or provider-mixing risk.

recommendation.title: Add narrow identity repair or migration
recommendation.body: Implement a tested repair path for known-safe CLI/runtime providerKey and scopeHash drift while preserving hard failure for genuinely incompatible indexes.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz introduced the identity validation behavior and is the clearest history-linked owner for the policy boundary.
